title: Agent Comparison Telemetry Event v0.2
description: One record per (question, agent variant, model config) execution. This is a MEASUREMENT record for cross-Agent/cross-model comparison -- it is never a Gold record, is never hand-authored, and must never be promoted into domain/evaluation Gold artifacts. answer_text is retained only as the measured output of one run, not as a reference answer. Turn P1.1: replaces v0.1's citation_accuracy (which actually measured Validator proof-issuance rate, not citation correctness) with evidence_validation_success_rate (the same Runtime-proof measurement, honestly named) plus citation_binding_status/unsupported_claim_count (a real post-generation grounding check of the model's OWN claims -- see domain/agent-comparison/flows/hard-claim-grounding.mjs) and model_call_attempt_count/success_count/failure_count/model_fallback_used/model_failure_code/scoring_eligible (so a model failure or a fallback substitution can never be silently counted as a normal model success). Actual citation ACCURACY against Gold remains the responsibility of a separate Gold-based scorer -- this event never claims to measure that.

validation_status.description: Mirrors ValidationResult.answerability (domain/runtime/agent-runtime.mjs) plus NO_CLAIM_MADE for a run that produced no final_response.answer to validate at all.

evidence_validation_success_rate.description: Runtime measurement, NOT a citation-accuracy score: successful validateEvidence calls / total validateEvidence attempts this request (domain/runtime/agent-runtime.mjs's Validator). This only tells you the proof-issuance rate against the trusted EvidenceStore -- it says nothing about whether the model's ANSWER TEXT actually cited its evidence correctly (see citation_binding_status/unsupported_claim_count for that) or whether the answer matches Gold (a separate, Gold-based scorer's responsibility). null when the run made zero validateEvidence attempts (nothing to score).
evidence_validation_success_rate.$comment: Renamed from v0.1's citation_accuracy, which was mislabeled -- same underlying computation, honest name.

citation_binding_status.description: Result of post-generation grounding verification on the model's OWN generated answer (see hard-claim-grounding.mjs). PASS: the model-generated answer's used_fact_ids/used_evidence_ids were all authorized+validated this request, and every extracted hard claim (number/date/document id) in its text was found in the grounded Fact/Evidence data -- the generated answer was kept. FAIL: at least one citation or hard claim did not check out -- the generated answer was DISCARDED and replaced with a deterministic grounded fallback. NOT_CHECKED: there was no model-generated text to check at all (no model call was attempted, or the call itself failed before producing any text).

unsupported_claim_count.description: Count of hard claims (number/date/document id) extracted from a model-generated answer that could not be matched against this request's grounded Fact/Evidence data. Always 0 when citation_binding_status is PASS or NOT_CHECKED.

model_call_attempt_count.description: Incremented the instant a ModelAdapter.generate() call starts, before success/failure is known. Always equals model_call_success_count + model_call_failure_count (domain/agent-comparison/telemetry.mjs's instrumentModelAdapter enforces this by construction).

model_fallback_used.description: true when a deterministic fallback answer was substituted for a model-generated one, for ANY reason (the model call itself failed, or its generated answer failed post-generation citation-binding/hard-claim verification). false both when a genuine model-generated answer was used AND when no model call was ever attempted at all (e.g. an honest information-limit answer with zero grounded facts) -- model_call_attempt_count distinguishes those two false cases.

model_failure_code.description: The stable failure code of the LAST failed ModelAdapter.generate() call this request, or null if every attempted call succeeded (including when zero calls were attempted). Never a raw provider error message or any value that could contain an API key.

scoring_eligible.description: false whenever model_fallback_used is true -- a fallback-substituted answer must never be scored as if it reflected the configured model's own quality. true for both a genuine model-generated (and grounding-verified) answer and a legitimate zero-model-call information-limit answer. A structured-retrieval/grounding regression check MAY still use a scoring_eligible=false row; a model-quality comparison MUST NOT.
